title: Are ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude Really Free? The Real Calculation of Hidden Costs
excerpt: Can you really get by without spending money using ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or Perplexity? Or do you have to buy a subscription to get good features? Let's clear up the misconceptions and understand the reality.
author: Admin
caption: The real picture of free vs. paid plans of AI tools

body.x: Nowadays, with AI you can do almost everything—from writing, image creation, video editing, research to coding. But a question comes to many minds: Can AI tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or Perplexity really be used for free? Or do you have to pay to use good features? Let's go beyond common assumptions and understand the matter realistically!
ChatGPT

Using ChatGPT's free version, you can do things like getting answers to questions, writing, information search, file analysis, and image creation. However, not all features are always equally available. There may be limits on using advanced models and some features.
**Reality:** There are both Free and Paid plans. You don't need to spend money right away just for general tasks.
🔗 Official website: https://chatgpt.com/
Google Gemini

With Google Gemini, you can answer questions, write, generate ideas, do research, and various creative tasks. Quite a few benefits are available even in the free plan. However, for advanced models, more usage opportunities, or certain premium features, a paid plan may be needed.
**Reality:** You can start with free; if you want more benefits, you can consider a paid plan.
🔗 Official website: https://gemini.google.com/
Claude AI

Claude AI can be used for writing, understanding long documents, coding, generating ideas, and analyzing complex topics. It has a free plan. However, there are usage limits, and if you work heavily on a regular basis, a paid plan may be needed.
**Reality:** You can start with the free plan, but heavy use may cost money.
🔗 Official website: https://claude.ai/
Perplexity AI

Perplexity AI is popular for finding information from the web and getting answers with the help of various sources. Its free plan offers general search opportunities. However, advanced search, more Pro Searches, and some premium benefits may be limited or paid.
**Reality:** For general information search, the free plan may be enough for many.
🔗 Official website: https://www.perplexity.ai/
Keep the following points in mind to understand easily

items: ✅ Free Plan: Can be used without money, but there may be usage limits.
✅ Freemium Model: Some benefits are free, and you have to pay for advanced benefits.
✅ Paid Subscription: By paying a certain fee, you get more usage or additional benefits.
✅ API Pricing: If developers add an AI model to their own app or website, there may be separate costs based on usage.

body.x: Remember, just because a tool has a free plan doesn't mean all its features are free. And just because there's a paid plan doesn't mean the free version is useless—that's not the case.
What to verify before spending money

items: 🔹 Whether the feature you need is available in the free plan.
🔹 How many times you can use it per day or month.
🔹 Whether payment is possible from Bangladesh.
🔹 How much the displayed price will be in Bangladeshi Taka and whether extra charges apply.
🔹 If any website claims lifetime free use, whether that claim has been verified.

body.x: The most important thing: Don't buy a paid subscription just following trends. First try the free version, then decide according to your needs.
Which tool should you start with?
You can start with ChatGPT or Gemini for general writing and daily tasks. You can try Claude for writing and coding. And you can try Perplexity for information search with sources.
However, AI answers are not always accurate. I think it's wise to verify important information from other reliable sources.

Which AI tools are you currently using or using more? 1. ChatGPT 2. Google Gemini 3. Claude AI 4. Perplexity AI 5. Any other AI tool—write the name of your favorite tool in the comments. Your experience can help others choose the right AI tool too.
So, stay connected with Admin to know essential information about AI technology and the digital world.

title: No Need to Install an App to Scan QR Codes Anymore
excerpt: Camera, Google Lens, Quick Settings shortcut, or gallery—easy techniques to scan QR codes without any separate app.
author: Admin
caption: Easy ways to scan QR codes without additional apps

body.x: In shops, on restaurant menus, in payments—QR codes are everywhere now. Yet many still have a separate "QR Scanner" app installed, half of which are full of ads. But your phone already has the capability to do this.
Scan with the camera itself

On most Android phones (Android 9 or later), just open the camera app and point it at the QR code. Keep the code inside the frame and hold still for a second or two—a link will appear on the screen. Tap it and you'll reach the destination. No need to take a photo.
If the camera doesn't work, use Google Lens

Look for the Lens icon in the camera app, or open the Google app and tap the Lens icon next to the search bar. Point it at the code—Lens will show the link itself. My old phone's camera didn't scan directly; I used to manage with Lens.
Shortcut from Quick Settings
Pull down the notification shade twice to open Quick Settings. Many phones have a "Scan QR code" tile there. If not, tap the pencil icon and add the tile—then it's one tap to the scanner.
QR code in an image?
If someone sends a QR code image on WhatsApp, open it in Google Photos and tap the Lens icon at the bottom. The code inside the image will also be scanned. The same trick works for screenshots.
Two important things

One—if scanning fails, wipe the camera lens once and check if the lighting is okay. Two—before tapping the link, read the URL once. A QR code itself is harmless, but where it's taking you is the real thing. Never give your password or OTP on an unknown, suspicious link.

title: Phone Running Slow? Remove Unused Apps and Free Up Space
excerpt: Pick out apps you haven't opened in months and uninstall them, keep auto-archive on—your phone will be lighter and storage will be freed.
author: Admin
caption: Ways to free up phone storage by removing unused apps

body.x: One day I noticed I had about 140 apps on my phone. Yet I regularly use at most 20-25. The rest? Installed at some point thinking "might be useful," then forgotten. Your phone surely has such apps too. Let's do a little cleaning today.
See which apps you don't use
Go to Settings → Apps; many phones have a "Sort by last used" or "Sort by size" option. Those you haven't opened in months are your targets.

If you want an easier route, open the Files by Google app (available on most phones by default). Going to the Clean tab will show a "Delete unused apps" suggestion—the phone itself tells you which apps have been unused for months. Select them one by one and tap Uninstall. Done.
If you don't want to delete—auto-archive

There's an auto-archive option in Play Store settings—keeping it on makes rarely used apps automatically "archive" and free up space, but your data and settings remain. When needed later, just tap the icon and it downloads again.
One caution

Going into an app's settings and pressing "Clear cache" is safe, but don't press "Clear data" or "Clear storage"—that will erase all app data and you'll be logged out too. And for apps that come pre-installed with the phone and can't be deleted, keep them Disabled—out of sight is a lot of peace of mind.
That day I removed about 30 apps and got about 4 GB of space. The phone seemed to breathe a little lighter too. Your turn.

title: Chrome Tab Groups: Organize Tab Clutter with Names and Colors
excerpt: If you keep 15-20 tabs open at once, use tab groups to separate work and study tabs. Step-by-step guide.
author: Admin
caption: Guide to organizing tab clutter with Chrome tab groups

body.x: When 15-20 tabs are open at once, it becomes hard to tell which is which in the tab bar. Each tab becomes so small that only the icon is visible. With Chrome's Tab Groups feature, you can organize similar tabs into a group with a name and color—like office work tabs in one group, study tabs in another. In today's post, I'll show step by step how to create tab groups in desktop Chrome, add/remove tabs, close and save groups, and the difference between Delete and Ungroup.
How to create a new tab group

items: Right-click on any tab.
Go to Add tab to group from the menu, then select New group.
A colored circle will appear to the left of the tab. Right-click on that circle or the group name again to name the group and choose your preferred color.
From the same menu, you can also add new tabs to the group or remove the group.

body.x: Adding or removing tabs from a group

To add: drag the tab with the mouse and drop it inside the group. To remove: right-click on the tab and select Remove from group. For multiple tabs at once: hold Ctrl and select each tab; for adjacent tabs, click the first tab, hold Shift, and click the last tab. Then right-click on any selected tab and choose Add tabs to group.
Close groups to keep the tab bar empty

Not needed now, but don't want to lose the tabs? Right-click on the group and select Close group. The group isn't deleted—it's saved in the bookmarks bar or Chrome menu's Tab groups option. To reopen, click the Grid icon in the bookmarks bar and select the group name, or go to the top-right More (⋮) menu → Tab groups and choose the group.

Go to Settings → Appearance and enable Show tab groups in bookmarks bar to keep saved groups always visible in the bookmarks bar. Enabling Automatically pin new tab groups to the bookmarks bar makes a new group pin to the bookmarks bar as soon as it's created—even groups created on another device with the same Google account will appear here.
Know the difference between Delete and Ungroup

items: Ungroup: Tabs remain open as before, only the group breaks apart.
Delete group: The group is deleted from your device as well as from other devices signed in with the same Google account. Think before confirming.
Close group: All tabs in the group close, so save important work first.

body.x: Remember: if signed in with the same Google account, Delete or Ungroup changes apply across all devices. Keep your tab bar clean with this built-in Chrome feature without any extension.

title: Don't Like Your Phone's Default Camera-Gallery? Check Out These Two Open Source Apps

caption: Finding open source camera and gallery apps

body.x: Phone camera hardware is getting better day by day, but the default camera and gallery apps that come with it often disappoint—one lacks manual controls, the other is busy uploading to the cloud instead of organizing photos. Last year on a tour I realized that to take good photos, you also need a good camera app. In the open source world, these two apps are at the top of my favorite list.
Open Camera

A years-old, experienced-developer-made open source camera app that still receives regular updates. The auto-stabilize feature is great—photos come out straight even if your hand shakes. ISO, exposure, white balance, focus—everything can be set manually. Scene mode, timer, face detection are also available. For those whose phone's default camera app lacks a pro mode, this is the best gift. Download: https://f-droid.org/packages/net.sourceforge.opencamera/
Aves Libre

And for gallery, there's Aves Libre. title: Keep Notes Your Way: Two Free and Open Source Note Apps
excerpt: Markor and Joplin—your notes stay with you, no lock-in, and sync if needed.
author: Admin
caption: Freedom to keep notes: Markor and Joplin

body.x: Do you keep notes on your phone? Shopping lists, work ideas, study points—note apps are invaluable for remembering small things. But ask yourself one question: where do your notes actually live? In many popular note apps, notes mean data stored on their servers. I want my writing to stay with me, so I've leaned toward open source.
If you want simple, fast notes: Markor

Markor is a plain-text and Markdown editor. That means your notes are saved as ordinary text files on your phone—no lock-in, can be opened in any editor. Runs completely offline, can make to-do lists in todo.txt format, has syntax highlighting, and can export to HTML or PDF if desired. No ads, doesn't ask for unnecessary permissions either. Download: https://f-droid.org/packages/net.gsantner.markor/
If you want sync across all devices: Joplin

Joplin is somewhat of an open source alternative to Evernote. Notebooks, tags, full-text search—everything is there. Its best aspect is sync: Nextcloud, Dropbox, OneDrive, or WebDAV—you can sync notes to your preferred place, and enable end-to-end encryption if desired. Runs on Windows, Linux, Android, iOS—almost all platforms, so you can write on your phone and read on your computer. Download: https://f-droid.org/packages/net.cozic.joplin/
My own experience: when changing my old phone, I just copied Markor's text files to the new phone—all notes appeared without any export-import hassle. This freedom is the real fun of open source.

title: The Real Price of Free Apps Is Your Data: Two Open Source Tools to Block Trackers
excerpt: Blokada and TrackerControl—filter traffic locally to stop ads and tracking, your data doesn't leave your device.
author: Admin
caption: Open source solutions for blocking trackers

body.x: A few months ago I installed a free puzzle game—it was fun to play. A few days later I noticed that even when not playing the game, my phone's data was being consumed and the battery was draining fast. Later I learned that multiple trackers were hidden inside that game—quietly sending my usage information to advertising companies. The real price of free apps is actually our data.
The good news is there are open source ways to stop this tracking. Both apps use the phone's VPN feature to filter traffic locally—your data doesn't go to any external server, and no root is needed.
Blokada

System-wide ad and tracker blocker. Once enabled, it blocks ads and tracking requests in browsers, games, all apps. Also does DNS filtering, providing some protection from malicious sites too. Setup is almost zero—install and press one button to start. Download: https://f-droid.org/packages/org.blokada.alarm
TrackerControl

This goes one step further. It shows you in front of your eyes which app is sending what data to which company—by name. Then you decide which trackers to block and which to keep. Started as a research project at Oxford University, this app is completely open source, so its claims can be verified. Download: https://f-droid.org/packages/net.kollnig.missioncontrol.fdroid

An important note: on Android, only one VPN app can run at a time, so don't run Blokada and TrackerControl together—choose one. And some banking apps may complain when VPN is on; temporarily turning it off is enough then.

title: Who's Watching Your Typing? Two Privacy-Friendly Open Source Keyboards - Admin
excerpt: FlorisBoard and HeliBoard—open source keyboards that run completely offline, where your typing data doesn't go anywhere.
author: Admin

title: Why Doesn't Android Run Linux Software Despite Standing on Linux? - Admin
excerpt: Linux kernel vs. distribution, ART vs. glibc, security model—explanation of why desktop Linux software doesn't run directly on Android.
author: Admin
caption: Explanation of Android and Linux software compatibility

body.x: Android has a Linux kernel inside—hearing this, many think, then Linux software must run on Android too! But in reality, that doesn't happen. To understand why, you need to know the difference between the Linux kernel and a Linux distribution.
Linux kernel vs. Linux distribution

The Linux kernel is the core part of the system—the bridge between hardware and software. But to make a usable operating system, you need system tools, libraries, software, and a user environment alongside the kernel. Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Linux Mint—these are distributions. On the other hand, Android also uses the Linux kernel, but it has its own system services, libraries, app framework, and Android Runtime (ART).
Key differences

items: App runtime: Android apps are usually written in Kotlin/Java and run through ART; Linux software directly uses system calls and libraries.
System libraries: Android uses Bionic, Linux distributions usually use glibc.
Graphical environment: Android has its own system; Linux has GNOME, KDE Plasma, Xfce, etc.
Security and permission model: Android uses sandboxing, Linux uses user/process permissions.

body.x: Yet cross-running is possible

To run Linux software on Android, you can use Termux and proot-based Debian/Ubuntu environments. For graphical apps, an additional display environment may be needed; root isn't always required. Conversely, to run Android apps on desktop Linux, you can use Waydroid (container-based) or Android Emulator.
However, whether it will work depends on hardware, distribution, kernel configuration, and software compatibility.

title: Internet Without Chrome? Check Out These Open Source Browsers - Admin
excerpt: Firefox, Fennec F-Droid, and IronFox—guide to switching from Chrome to open source browsers for privacy and transparency.
author: Admin
caption: Open source browser alternatives to Chrome

body.x: Using Chrome means creating the possibility that your browsing data goes to Google. For privacy and transparency, many are now leaning toward open source browsers, because their code can be publicly audited—hidden data collection is nearly impossible. Here I'll talk about three browsers.
Firefox

Open source under MPL-2.0 license. Full extension support on mobile—including uBlock Origin. Enhanced Tracking Protection is on by default. Sync tabs, passwords, bookmarks between phone and computer. Download: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.mozilla.firefox
Fennec F-Droid

A clean build of Firefox made by the F-Droid community—without proprietary code and telemetry, runs without Google Play Services. Updates with new Firefox releases. Download: https://f-droid.org/packages/org.mozilla.fennec_fdroid/
IronFox

Community successor to the discontinued Mull. Firefox-based, with security and privacy hardening. Deep customization possible via about:config on mobile, which is locked in regular Firefox mobile. Not in main F-Droid; must install from its own repository. Details: https://ironfoxoss.org/docs/installation/
Try any one for a week—the author thinks you won't want to return to Chrome after that.

title: Gmail Storage Full? Ways to Save Space Without Spending Money - Admin
excerpt: Gmail, Drive, and Photos together are only 15 GB—ways to free up space easily without buying anything.
author: Admin
caption: Gmail storage full? Ways to free up space without cost

body.x: Gmail storage full—seeing this message, many rush to buy Google One. But in just a few steps, it's possible to free up a lot of space without spending a penny. Remember, Gmail, Google Drive, and Google Photos—all three together are only 15 GB of free storage.
Step 1: Find large attachments
In Gmail's search bar, type: has:attachment larger:10M. This will show emails with attachments larger than 10 megabytes. To filter further, use larger:5M or before:2024/01/01.
Step 2: Delete old promotional and social emails
Search: category:promotions older_than:1y and category:social older_than:1y. Select many emails at once and delete.
Step 3: Empty Trash and Spam
Deleted emails also stay in Trash and consume storage. Go to Trash and press "Empty Trash now". Empty the Spam folder too.
Step 4: Unsubscribe from unnecessary newsletters
There's an Unsubscribe option next to the sender's name, or use Manage Subscriptions. Stop recurring junk mail.
Step 5: Back up important attachments before deleting
Back up important files to Drive or your computer, then delete the emails.
Just by deleting large attachments, the author got about 4 GB of space.

author: Admin
caption: Guide to earning by writing on Ami Poddoja

body.x: Love to write? It's possible to earn online by writing Bengali stories, essays, novels—without any initial investment. By registering as a writer on the Ami Poddoja app/website and publishing books, you can earn based on views. Here's the complete process step by step.
Registration

Create an account on the Ami Poddoja website with correct information—name, address, password, mobile, email. You may need to provide an NID photo or Facebook profile link if required. Writer accounts are usually approved within 2–3 hours.
Add payment information
Add payment information via bank, bKash, Nagad, or Upay and cross-check it, so there's no problem withdrawing earnings.
Enable monetization
Go to the Monetization section and manually enable monetization.
Earning model

items: 50 Taka for the first 5,000 views.
10 Taka per 1,000 views after that (rates may be changed by the site authority).
Minimum withdrawal is 200 Taka.
Payment is given automatically once a month.

body.x: Content types
Various types of content can be published—short stories, essays, novels, romantic novels, erotic novels, BTS stories, e-books, poetry books.
Originality
Content must be your own original work. Publishing the same book on another website may result in payment cancellation. Sharing on social media is allowed.
Steps to publish a book

First create a book (unique name, category, description, cover, 18+ mark)—send for admin approval. Then add chapters (minimum 1,000 words per chapter). The first 5 chapters require admin approval; subsequent chapters are published directly.
Promotion
Share your book link on social media and leave constructive comments on others' books—this increases views and earnings.
For support, WhatsApp: 16812767381

title: Follow These 10 Rules Online to Stay Safe from Hacking - Admin
excerpt: Passwords, 2FA, OTP, public WiFi, updates—10 practical rules to avoid hacking, follow them yourself and teach your family.
author: Admin
caption: 10 rules to stay safe online

body.x: Most hacking incidents happen because the user themselves opens the door—using the same password repeatedly, clicking suspicious links, sharing OTPs. An acquaintance's Facebook account was hacked because they logged in through a "win free recharge" link. Following the 10 rules below can greatly reduce the risk.
1. Use a unique password for every important account
Using the same password everywhere means if one place leaks, all accounts are at risk. If it's hard to remember, use a password manager.
2. Enable Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)
Keep 2FA enabled on email, banking, and social media—even if the password is stolen, the account stays safe.
3. Never share OTP or verification codes
Banks never ask for OTP over the phone. If someone asks, understand it's fraud.
4. Verify the sender's address before clicking links
"Take action now or your account will be closed"—such urgent messages are suspicious. Check the real sender's address.
5. Avoid banking/payments on public WiFi
Use a VPN if necessary.
6. Keep your phone, apps, and browser updated
Updates close security vulnerabilities.
7. Don't share your address, phone number, or travel plans on social media
Thieves also look at Facebook.
8. Review app permissions
If a flashlight app asks for contacts, that's a red flag.
9. Check bank statements and account activity once a month
If you see unknown transactions, inform the bank.
10. Teach these rules to elderly and child family members
They are the main targets of fraud. Online safety isn't a one-day task, it's a habit.

title: Know the Legal Ways to Watch YouTube Offline - Admin
excerpt: Browser download, downloading your own videos as MP4 from YouTube Studio, Premium's Smart Downloads—legal ways to watch offline.
author: Admin
caption: Legal ways to watch YouTube offline

body.x: Many people use third-party downloaders to watch YouTube without internet, which isn't legal. But YouTube itself provides several legal ways to watch offline. Here I'll discuss those.
Method 1: Download from desktop browser

Videos can be downloaded from youtube.com in Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Opera. However, downloaded videos aren't saved as separate files—they stay inside the YouTube app and occasionally expire if no internet connection is available.
Method 2: Download your own uploaded videos as MP4
Go to YouTube Studio → Content tab → three-dot menu → Download/Save to Device. A great way for backup.
Method 3: Premium's Smart Downloads
In YouTube Premium settings, go to Background & downloads and enable Smart Downloads. When on WiFi, YouTube will automatically download your favorite videos. Check once before your journey.
The author is using Premium's free trial for a trip.
